4.0.0.en: 1 Hear this word, ye kine of Bashan, that are in the mountain of Samaria, which oppress the poor, which crush the needy, which say to their masters, "Bring, and let us drink." 2 The Lord GOD hath sworn by his holiness, "Lo, the days shall come upon you, that he will take you away with hooks, and your posterity with fishhooks. 3 And ye shall go out at the breaches, every cow at that which is before her; and ye shall cast them into the palace, saith the LORD."

4.0.1.en: "Hear this word, ye kine of Bashan, that are in the mountain of Samaria, which oppress the poor, which crush the needy, which say to their masters, Bring, and let us drink" [1].

4.0.2.en: "Bashan" is a Hebrew name meaning "level or smooth land." It referred to the half-tribe of Manasseh (Deut 3:13), and lies in the land of Canaan east of the Jordan between Mount Hermon and Gilead (Num 21:33); its soil is exceedingly fertile and its water abundant. It is mentioned in the Holy Bible about 60 times. It was known for its herds (Ps 22:12; Ezek 39:18), which were marked by much fat (Deut 32:14), and was famous for its evergreen oak forests (Isa 2:13; Ezek 27:6; Zech 11:2) down to this day.

4.0.3.en: Here the Lord likens the people of Israel to the fat and strong cows of Bashan, which graze in rich pastures, and which were marked by their injustice to the poor and their crushing of the needy. The rich of the people and its nobles grazed amid excessive wealth, seizing everything for themselves. And instead of helping the needy and the oppressed, they exploit their poverty, misery and helplessness in order to crush them all the more with injustice and tyranny, so that the rich grows richer in his riches, and the poor in his poverty and misery.

4.0.4.en: These rich men go to masters as unjust as themselves and say: "Bring, and let us drink," that is, let us get drunk with you in your feasts and enjoy pleasures and lusts amid the crushing of the needy and the tears of the oppressed, as though they find no pleasure in drunkenness unless they mix it with tears and blend it with injustice. As the wise man says: "So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and from the hand of their oppressors there was oppression" (Eccl 1:4).

4.0.5.en: Some see that the cows of Bashan here are none other than the Israelite women, who had become fat from the multitude of feasts and a life of excessive luxury, and violent. These women who dwell in Samaria ask their men, that is, their masters or "baals" (husbands), to fulfill for them what the great Baal requires. Since the worship of Baal consists essentially of flagrant drunkenness, these "baals" provide drink for their women. It is as though the cows of Bashan are chiefly responsible for the injustice that falls on the poor and the needy, because they incite their husbands to it in order to fulfill their passing pleasures, especially constant, unceasing drunkenness!

4.0.6.en: What does God do with these unjust cows?

4.1.0.en: The Lord GOD hath sworn by his holiness: "Lo, the days shall come upon you, that he will take you away with hooks (a hook or grapnel), and your posterity with fishhooks. And ye shall go out at the breaches, every cow at that which is before her; and ye shall cast them into the palace (the fortress, Hermon), saith the LORD" [2-3].

4.1.1.en: What does the Lord do with them?

4.1.2.en: First: The Lord swears by His holiness that He intervenes because of what the cows of Bashan did to His needy and poor children in order to fulfill their drinking and pleasures; so He takes them away with hooks, as the Lord says to Sennacherib king of Assyria by the mouth of Isaiah: "Because thy rage against me and thy tumult is come up into mine ears, therefore I will put my hook in thy nose, and my bridle in thy lips, and I will turn thee back by the way by which thou camest" (Isa 37:29; 2 Kgs 19:28).

4.1.3.en: It seems that the hook was put in the nose of a violent animal in order to drag it in humiliation, especially wild animals such as lions. Therefore it was used to drag captives, especially kings, to humiliate them, as the king of Assyria did to Manasseh (2 Chr 33:11). Since the cows of Bashan raged against the poor for the sake of their pleasures, God drags them away as captives; He seizes them and puts hooks in their noses so that they become captives without honor, authority or strength!

4.1.4.en: The world in its pleasures plays with man and makes him like a wild animal, thinking that no one escapes from his hands and fangs, but he soon finds himself led in humiliation to where he tastes the fruit of his injustice.

4.1.5.en: Second: The chastisement does not stop at the cows, but He catches their children like fish with the fishhook! Man in his revelry prepares loss, even destruction, for his children as well.

4.1.6.en: If the children of Israel represent the human soul, then their women, that is, the cows of Bashan, point to the body, which falls in humiliation with the soul and is shattered, while the children point to man's gifts, which go down with sin, so that man loses his spirit, his body and all his gifts and energies because of sin. On the contrary, the soul of the righteous rejoices, his body is sanctified and his gifts grow, as the psalmist says: "Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine by the sides of thine house: thy children like olive plants round about thy table. Behold, that thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the LORD" (Ps 128:3-4). He is blessed, and his wife and his children, that is, his soul, his body and all his gifts!

4.1.7.en: Third: Each cow goes out at the breaches straight before her, to rush into the fortress, or the palace, or Hermon (according to the Greek text). Perhaps the breaches occurred in the walls, since the cows of Bashan, by their injustice and uncleanness, refused to remain within the walls of the divine commandment, and fled through the breaches so as not to meet the commandment, and rushed to the palace they had made for themselves, or the fortress that is the work of their hands, hoping that it might be able to protect them, as man did of old when he tried to build the tower of Babel to hide in it from the face of God at the Flood!

4.1.8.en: If the Greek text mentions "Hermon" instead of the fortress, perhaps the breaches here mean that the cows of Bashan who did injustice against the needy fall into captivity when the walls of Samaria are split and collapse. They then find no escape but are taken into captivity as to slaughter, and the enemy takes them to Hermon, where the captivity is, or to the palace or the fortress, to remain there as humiliated captives.

4.2.s.en: 2. The rejection of worship joined with injustice:

4.2.0.en: 4 "Come to Bethel, and transgress; at Gilgal multiply transgression; and bring your sacrifices every morning, and your tithes every three days: 5 And offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving with leaven, and proclaim and publish the free offerings: for this liketh you, O ye children of Israel, saith the Lord GOD.

4.2.1.en: Perhaps the children of Israel think that these warnings do not concern them, for they go to Bethel to offer sacrifices every morning, and pay their tithes every three days without delay, and offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving to God... In their own eyes they are lovers of God, offering Him gifts and offerings without number!

4.2.2.en: How easy it is for man to deceive himself, treating his evil not by repentance and returning to God but by stopping at some outward forms of worship, so that they deprive the ritual of the Church of its spirit by isolating it from the practical life of faith, and distort the offerings and gifts by presenting them without the heart!

4.2.3.en: "Come to Bethel, and transgress; at Gilgal multiply transgression" [4].

4.2.4.en: The Lord says this in the language of irony, for they commit all evils and injustices and go to the holy places and fill them... as though they were a people marked by religiosity and spirituality! They go to holy things while not holy. They visit the house of God and do not return to God Himself! Therefore He says to them: "transgress... and multiply transgression," as though He were saying: if your many visits to the holy places are a cover for your hidden evils, you are adding sin to sin, and treating wounds with more dangerous wounds!

4.2.5.en: "Bring your sacrifices every morning, and your tithes every three days" [4].

4.2.6.en: The Jew was bound to offer a yearly sacrifice (1 Sam 1:3, 7, 21), and to present the accounts of his tithes every three years (Deut 14:28; 26:12). If the unjust man offers a daily sacrifice instead of the yearly one, and gives his tithes every three days instead of every three years, he is not accepted by God... For God is not bribed by offerings and money, but seeks the spirit of the gift, the inner fruit in the heart, not the gift in itself. As St. Paul says to the people of Philippi, who were full of love: "Ye sent once and again unto my necessity. Not because I desire a gift: but I desire fruit that may abound to your account" (Phil 4:16-17). For this very reason the same Apostle warns us against giving without love, saying: "And though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing" (1 Cor 13:3).

4.3.0.en: "And offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving with leaven, and proclaim and publish the free offerings: for this liketh you, O ye children of Israel, saith the Lord GOD" [5]. It is as though He says: if you come to my house and my holy places, and offer sacrifices and pay tithes, you have loved to provoke me, for you offer leaven as a thank offering, and the free offerings to my house. The Law forbade offering leaven: "No meat offering, which ye shall bring unto the LORD, shall be made with leaven: for ye shall burn no leaven, nor any honey, in any offering of the LORD made by fire" (Lev 2:11). Leaven signified the evil that spreads like leaven in the dough; thus, while they present the offerings, they carry their evil in the midst of them, as though it were a thank offering... though in reality it is an offering of provocation to the Lord.

4.3.1.en: In the Septuagint: "They read the Law outside, and call to public assemblies." Perhaps He means by this that they pretend to religiosity by speaking about the divine Law with unbelievers, and argue with them about it with great zeal, and confirm this zeal by calling to public assemblies. In contrast, they do not carry the Law in their hearts within, and they have no personal relationship with God! This is the most dangerous form of religiosity, when it is all poured into zeal without inner life, and into participation in communal worship and religious celebrations without the hidden relationship with God in the soul or in the closet! This is what the children of Israel loved, as the Lord says.

4.4.0.en: 6 "And I also have given you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and want of bread in all your places: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the LORD. 7 And also I have withholden the rain from you, when there were yet three months to the harvest: and I caused it to rain upon one city, and caused it not to rain upon another city: one piece was rained upon, and the piece whereupon it rained not withered. 8 So two or three cities wandered unto one city, to drink water; but they were not satisfied: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the LORD. 9 I have smitten you with blasting and mildew: when your gardens and your vineyards and your fig trees and your olive trees increased, the palmerworm devoured them: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the LORD. 10 I have sent among you the pestilence after the manner of Egypt: your young men have I slain with the sword, and have taken away your horses; and I have made the stink of your camps to come up unto your nostrils: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the LORD. 11 I have overthrown some of you, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and ye were as a firebrand plucked out of the burning: yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the LORD.

4.4.1.en: He enumerated for them the chastisements that He allowed them to fall under, and yet they did not benefit from them, for each time He punishes, saying: "Yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the LORD" [6, 8-11]. It is as though chastisement in the eyes of God is not vengeance for Himself but love... He desires man's return to Him.

4.5.0.en: If the previous chastisements, with all their multitude and variety, did not achieve their goal because of the hardness of man's heart, then He is bound to present a harsher chastisement, so that man may recover from his drunkenness, come to know God and prepare to meet Him: "And because I will do this unto thee, prepare to meet thy God, O Israel" [12]. Perhaps this phrase is the key to the whole book, indeed the key to the whole Holy Bible: all that God does with His people, whether kindness or firmness, leniency or severity, is so that it may prepare to meet its God, who comes down to it to dwell in it and to sanctify it as a people for Himself!

4.5.1.en: What are the chastisements that God allowed to His people?

4.5.2.en: "And I also have given you cleanness (idleness, or ceasing from work) of teeth in all your cities, and want of bread in all your places" [6]. Their teeth became clean because they were deprived of chewing and eating, so that nothing at all entered their mouths! In the Septuagint: "Their teeth became idle, without work..." as though likened to the idle man who is of no use to himself or to others.

4.5.3.en: His saying "I have given you" indicates that what happens of natural disasters, which cause famines until their teeth become clean through disuse, does not happen by mere chance, but by a precise divine plan and a surpassing heavenly providence. Moreover, what happens is the gift of God, "I have given you": He bestows good things as He grants distress, trials and famines. In His love He is gentle with us and satisfies us, and in His wisdom He deprives us and chastises us so that we return to Him.

4.5.4.en: The trials and chastisements that He allows reveal by them the work of sin in us and its hidden fruit within us, for it causes:

4.5.5.en: First: famines, "want of bread in all your places" [6]. Perhaps He meant by it the famine that occurred in the days of the prophet Elisha and lasted seven years (2 Kgs 8:1). Thus sin drives to a spiritual famine, so that man is in want of spiritual bread in all his inner life. He lives without satisfaction, in a great emptiness that no one can fill except the Lord Himself, the Bread that came down from heaven (Jn 6:51).

4.5.6.en: Second: spiritual dryness. "And also I have withholden the rain from you, when there were yet three months to the harvest: and I caused it to rain upon one city, and caused it not to rain upon another city... So two or three cities wandered unto one city, to drink water; but they were not satisfied" [7-8]. When the soul rejects the fountain of living waters (Jer 2:13), that is, Christ the Savior, it is deprived of the rain of the Holy Spirit and remains in a state of dryness! Two neighboring cities, one of which is watered by the rain of the Spirit and the other dries up; two villages or fields in one city, one field watered by the grace of the Spirit and the other remaining dry! Thus the world includes various hearts: some that open to the gift of the fiery Spirit to be set aflame by Him and to bear the heavenly nature, and others that close in upon themselves to live in their dryness, dead in spirit, enjoying nothing but barrenness and destruction! As the Lord says: "Behold, my servants shall eat, but ye shall be hungry: behold, my servants shall drink, but ye shall be thirsty: behold, my servants shall rejoice, but ye shall be ashamed: Behold, my servants shall sing for joy of heart, but ye shall cry for sorrow of heart, and shall howl for vexation of spirit" (Isa 65:13-14).

4.5.7.en: What are the two or three cities that wandered to one city to drink water and were not satisfied but the foolish virgins who ask the wise ones for oil lest their lamps go out, and the wise answer: "Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you" (Mt 25:9), so they go outside the wedding and the door is shut against them!

4.5.8.en: Third: the smiting with destructive insects such as blasting, mildew and locusts, which eat the fruits of the soul, corrupt its inner garden and rule over its vines and fig trees... We have already spoken at greater length about the campaigns of the locusts, the vines and the fig trees in our study of the book of Joel.

4.5.9.en: If the soul is the inner paradise, or the garden in whose spiritual vines and fig trees God delights, then sin, like an insect, turns paradise into a wilderness and the fruit trees into a rugged waste!

4.5.10.en: Fourth: the pestilence that afflicts soul and body together, which puts man in a state of sickness, lying on his bed without strength and unable to work! He needs the Savior, the true Physician of the soul!

4.5.11.en: Fifth: the slaying of their young men with the sword, that is, the shattering of man's gifts (his children) and energies.

4.5.12.en: Sixth: the taking away of their horses. If the horse signifies strength and might, then when man commits sin he loses his mastery over himself and becomes a captive without strength or freedom of action!

4.5.13.en: Seventh: the stink of their camps coming up into their nostrils... Instead of man bearing the sweet fragrance of Christ, which gladdens the Father's heart and delights the heavenly ones, the stench of the odor of his own inner self wafts from man, as though he were a dead man who has begun to stink! He needs to hear the voice of our Lord Jesus: "Lazarus, come forth," and the dead man who stinks comes out of his tomb bearing the fragrance of life instead of death!

4.5.14.en: Eighth: destruction by earthquakes and volcanoes: "I have overthrown some of you, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and ye were as a firebrand plucked out of the burning" [11]. He threatened all by casting some into the fires through thunderbolts and volcanoes, and plucked some out that they might repent, yet they did not return to Him... Instead of volcanoes and thunderbolts destroying us with their deadly fires, we have need that the Lord enter into us, as on a swift, light cloud, to shatter our inner idols, burn our evils and set up in the midst of our heart an altar for Himself, as the prophet Isaiah said in speaking of the Lord who rides swiftly on the cloud to the land of Egypt (Isa 19:1).

4.5.15.en: These are the divine chastisements that exposed the work of sin in the heart, indeed in the whole man: spiritual hunger, dryness, attack by insects that spoil the fruit, infection with spiritual diseases, the shattering of gifts (the young men), deprivation of freedom (the taking away of the horses), the rising of the smell of corruption and stench, and destruction by the fires of deadly thunderbolts! But the purpose of these chastisements is: "Prepare to meet thy God, O Israel" [12].

4.6.0.en: 12 "Therefore thus will I do unto thee, O Israel: and because I will do this unto thee, prepare to meet thy God, O Israel." 13 For, lo, he that formeth the mountains, and createth the wind, and declareth unto man what is his thought, that maketh the morning darkness, and treadeth upon the high places of the earth, The LORD, The God of hosts, is his name.

4.7.0.en: God's chastisements exposed our corrupt state, as though by the surgeon's scalpel that opened the wound to reveal the stench hidden in the body. And now how is the wound to be bandaged, and our state mended? Or, as He said: how is "prepare to meet thy God, O Israel" to be fulfilled? He answers: "For, lo, he that formeth the mountains, and createth the wind (the Spirit), and declareth unto man what is his thought (his Christ), that maketh the morning darkness, and treadeth upon the high places of the earth, The LORD, The God of hosts, is his name" [13].

4.7.1.en: The Lord of glory says: "Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand?" (Lk 14:31). If Israel has entered into a dispute against God, let it know who God is and what His capabilities are, or else let it make peace with Him! Here the prophet declares that God is the maker of the mountains. If kings take refuge in firm mountains during war, God does not take refuge in them but is their Creator. As the psalmist says: "O LORD God of hosts, who is a strong LORD like unto thee? or to thy faithfulness round about thee? Thou rulest the raging of the sea: when the waves thereof arise, thou stillest them... The heavens are thine, the earth also is thine: as for the world and the fulness thereof, thou hast founded them" (Ps 89:8-11). If armies find their salvation in the mountains, God is the founder of the whole world.

4.7.2.en: He says: "createth the wind," and in the Septuagint "createth the spirit." The Creator of the wind, about which the army commander is concerned before the beginning of the battle, is God Himself.

4.7.3.en: He makes the dawn (the morning) darkness, because He sends His thick cloud, which covers the earth and hides the light, and He is the One who walks on the high places of the earth, or its lofty peaks... He is Yahweh, who cannot be comprehended or expressed! This is your God, whom you must prepare to meet, O Israel, not for dispute but for reconciliation!

4.7.4.en: The text came in the Septuagint thus: "He who establishes the thunder and creates the spirit and declares to man his Christ." Many of the Fathers, such as St. Augustine, see that this text carries a clear prophecy about the Messianic age, for the new Israel prepares to meet its God through the Father's declaring of His Christ to man, so that man receives Him as the mystery of reconciliation between the Father and man.

4.7.5.en: Some heretics tried to use this text to claim that the Holy Spirit is a creature, since it says "creates the spirit." Many of the Fathers answered them, among them St. Gregory, bishop of Nyssa, who says: [It is fitting for us to understand that the prophet speaks of the creation of another spirit in His establishing of the thunder, and not of the creation of the Holy Spirit. For the name "thunder" has been given in the mystical language of the Gospel. Those in whom faith in the Gospel is established without shaking pass from the flesh to the spirit, as the Lord says: "That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit" (Jn 3:6). It is God who establishes the voice of the Gospel and makes man spirit (spiritual); whoever is born of the Spirit and becomes spirit, to him Christ is declared, as the Apostle says: "No man can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by the Holy Ghost" (1 Cor 12:3).]

4.7.6.en: This is the secret of the new Israel's meeting: God establishes the thunder, that is, He sends us the word of preaching that thunders in the soul, and creates in us the spiritual nature instead of the fleshly life, so that Christ, the Lord of glory, is declared in us by His Holy Spirit!

4.7.7.en: By this the prophet turned the mind of Israel from the harsh chastisements, which could not bring them back to God but only exposed their weakness and the work of sin in them, to the Messiah the Savior, whom the Father declares to man, so that he receives Him by the Holy Spirit as Redeemer and Savior!
